title: Distinct distances in the body-centred cubic crystal
statement: Let the body-centred cubic crystal B_N be the points (x, y, z) with 0 <= x, y, z <= 2N - 2 whose coordinates are all even (the N^3 corners of an (N-1) x (N-1) x (N-1) block of cubes of edge 2) or all odd (the (N-1)^3 cube centres); squared distance dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, nearest neighbours at squared distance 3. Determine the largest number of points of the body-centred cubic crystal B_N such that all pairwise distances are different, as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 3; the headline cell is N = 5: find 9 or more such points of the region of side 5 (an upper bound is 10).
submission: Text file: one point 'x y z' per line, a point of the region of side 5 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 8 points of the region of side 5 with all pairwise distances different, the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: Erdos and Guy asked for the largest subset of the n x n grid (and of the d-dimensional grid) with all pairwise distances different, a discrete relative of Golomb rulers and of Erdos's distinct distances problem; for the square grid the answer is of order n^(2/3) up to logarithmic factors (Erdos-Guy, Lefmann-Thiele). Our problems tri-distinct and tetra-distinct ask it for the triangular grid and the tetrahedral (face-centred cubic) grid. The body-centred cubic crystal (iron, tungsten, the alkali metals) is the union of two cubic grids offset by half a cube diagonal; its squared distances (in units of half the cube edge) are the numbers x^2 + y^2 + z^2 with x, y, z all even or all odd, and the counting bound C(k, 2) <= (number of distances) gives k = O(N). How fast the largest distinct-distance sets grow is open.
references: P. Erdos, R. K. Guy, Distinct distances between lattice points, Elemente der Mathematik 25 (1970) 121-123
H. Lefmann, T. Thiele, Point sets with distinct distances, Combinatorica 15 (1995) 379-408

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: Erdos and Guy asked it for the d-dimensional grid and we for the triangular and tetrahedral grids (tri-distinct, tetra-distinct); no result was found for the body-centred cubic crystal, and it is not in the OEIS by name (too few exact values are known to search by terms).
closest: P. Erdos and R. K. Guy (1970): the square and d-dimensional grids.
Our problems tri-distinct (triangular grid) and tetra-distinct (tetrahedral grid): the same question in other lattices.
novelty.benchmark: no distinct-distance family in the benchmark

baseline.text: 8 for N = 5, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/bcc-distinct.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..3: 3, 5 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 5: 10 (the C(k, 2) distances are different among the 46 squared distances that occur in the region, so C(k, 2) <= 46).
